description: The supreme Jain mantra — bowing to the five supreme beings and the 9-line prayer that destroys all sins. It is the essence of Jain worship.
lyrics: Namo Arihantanam — I bow to the Arihants (liberated while embodied)
Namo Siddhanam — I bow to the Siddhas (fully liberated souls)
Namo Ayariyanam — I bow to the Acharyas (spiritual heads)
Namo Uvajjhayanam — I bow to the Upadhyayas (preceptors)
Namo Loye Savva Sahunam — I bow to all Sadhus (ascetics)
Eso Panch Namokkaro — These five salutations
Savva Papa Panasano — Destroy all sins
Mangalanam Cha Savvesim — Of all that is auspicious
Padhamam Havai Mangalam — This is the supreme
whenToChant: Morning upon waking, before meals, before meditation, during travel, before exams, before any important activity, at bedtime. Total recommended: 108 times daily minimum.
benefits: Destroys all sins, purifies speech, connects with supreme beings, creates protective vibration, removes obstacles, develops humility

description: The prayer of non-violence, seeking forgiveness from all living beings for any harm caused. It is the essence of Kshamavani.
lyrics: Khamemi Savva Jive — I forgive all living beings
Savve Jiva Khamantu Me — May all living beings forgive me
Mitti Me Savva Bhuesu — I have friendship with all
Veram Majjham Na Kenai — I have no enmity with anyone
translation: May all living beings forgive me
I have no enmity with anyone
whenToChant: Morning and evening; during Pratikramana; on Kshamavani day; when conflicts arise; before sleep.
benefits: Destroys karmic bondage from harm caused, creates inner peace, heals relationships, develops universal love, protects against negative karma

description: The 48-verse devotional hymn composed by Acharya Manatunga in praise of Lord Adinath (Rishabhdev). Each verse is believed to be composed while chained to a pillar, and each one caused a chain to break. Only selected verses are usually chanted by laypeople.
lyrics: Bhaktamara stotra verse 1: 'Devotional lotus of the lotus-footed Lord...'
Bhaktamara stotra verse 7: 'The lotus feet of the Lord destroy all obstacles...'
Bhaktamara stotra verse 14: 'Even the king of gods bows to your feet...'
Bhaktamara stotra verse 48: 'I take refuge in the lotus feet of Jinendra...'
translation: O Lord, your lotus feet are the supreme refuge
Your lotus feet destroy all karmic obstacles
Even heaven's king bows to your feet
I surrender at the feet of the conqueror
whenToChant: Morning Puja; during illness (for healing); before exams; during difficult times; temple worship.
benefits: Destroys obstacles, grants courage, develops bhakti, invokes divine protection, purifies the environment

description: A 44-verse devotional hymn to Lord Parshvanatha (23rd Tirthankara). Each verse describes his qualities and seeks his protection. The most widely recited Parshvanatha stotra.
lyrics: Uvassagharam — I take refuge in the Lord who destroyed delusion
Araham Uvajjhayanam — The Arihant, the omniscient teacher
Parshva Jinam Vandami — I bow to Parshvanatha, the ford-maker
Kshamavani Kshamavani — Forgiveness, forgiveness
translation: I take refuge in the Lord
whenToChant: Morning and evening; during Paryushan; before sleep; when seeking protection.
benefits: Develops forgiveness (Kshama), invites Parshvanatha's protection, destroys obstacles, creates inner peace

description: A 24-verse hymn describing the qualities of the 24 Tirthankaras and the universal dharma. It is recapitulated in the Samavayanga Sutra.
lyrics: Logassa — Obeisance to all Jinas of the past, present, and future
The 24 Tirthankaras establish dharma in every age cycle
Lord Rishabhdev taught the first codes of civilization
Lord Mahavira preached the supreme path of liberation
translation: Obeisance to all Jinas of past, present, and future
The 24 Tirthankaras establish dharma in every age cycle
Lord Rishabhdev taught the first codes
Lord Mahavira preached the supreme path
whenToChant: During temple worship; during Puja; in groups; morning.
benefits: Connects with all 24 Tirthankaras, receives blessings from universal dharma, develops devotion to all Jinas

description: The universal Jain greeting and greeting of victory to the Jinas. It is the opening and closing of every Jain gathering, Puja, and spiritual event.
lyrics: Jai Jinendra — Victory to the Lord of Conquerors
May the teachings of the Jina prevail
May Ahimsa guide all actions
May truth and non-violence reign
translation: Victory to the Lord of Conquerors
May the teachings of the Jina prevail
whenToChant: Morning greeting; before any gathering; at wedding ceremonies; at temple entry and exit.
benefits: Establishes sacred space, invokes Jina presence, aligns with spiritual community, marks auspicious moments
